items.text: **BoI circular deferring 447A to 19.10.2025.** Only a press report (Funder, 25 Sep 2025) was read; the regulatory impact report says "from 02/10/25, staged" and circular 2813 says six and ten months from 9 Apr 2025. Tried: web search; BoI HTML pages are Radware-blocked. Likely at boi.org.il/media/... as a circular "ח-06-28xx" from Sept 2025.

**Current versions of directives 447 and 417.** Read 447 v1 (5/24) and 417 v4 (5/24). Whether either was amended (for example 417 after s.5B2 took effect on 1.12.2025, or to cover FX deposits) is unknown. Tried: BoI directive list PDF (the media file returned was unrelated). Likely on the BoI "הוראות ניהול בנקאי תקין" page (blocked) or as new media PDFs.

**Consolidated disclosure rules after 2014.** The BoI copy lists amendments to 30.12.2014 only; later amendments (if any) to s.7-14, 30, 33B or Schedule E amounts not checked. Likely in Nevo or a newer BoI media PDF.

**Banking (Customer Service) Law consolidated text.** The BoI consolidation read is version 10/11; Amendments 37, 38, 39 were read separately from Reshumot; other amendments since 2011 (including s.16Y as now worded, and an amendment cited in the Amendment 41 bill as "התשפ"ו, עמ' 329") were not read. Knesset "נוסח לא רשמי" DOCX files exist but could not be parsed without a shell.

**Definition of "בנק בעל היקף פעילות קטן" (s.5B1(a)) and which banks are currently exempt from s.5B2.** Search budget ran out; the s.5B1 text was not read. Likely in the Amendment that added s.5B1 (Reshumot) or BoI guidance.

**Competition Authority decision text** (declaration and deposit directives, May 2026), its effective date, and the status of the five appeals at the Competition Tribunal. gov.il not reached; only press and the BoI statement read.
**Deposit-insurance bill P/6522/25**: status closed for now (on the table for preliminary discussion, unchanged since 2 Feb 2026). Watch for a preliminary-reading vote or a government bill.

**What BoI supervision protects in a bank failure.** No BoI or legislative text read states any guarantee, priority or compensation for depositors; BoI consumer pages are blocked. Likely in BoI FAQs (blocked) or the Banking Ordinance 1941 (s.8D authorised manager onward).

**Basic-track price cap.** The schedule marks the basic track "(בפיקוח)"; the controlling order and its current price were not read. Data-track item but the legal instrument should be cited in the rule base.
**Bank Esh Israel**: in the register with no website; whether it serves individuals and takes deposits. Tried: one web search, nothing found.
**One Zero and Bank of Jerusalem**: sites blocked (403 / Radware); product names, accountless-deposit terms and tariff location unverified.

**Savings plans**: whether each monthly instalment is a separate sub-deposit with its own lock-up and exit points, and how breaking a plan is priced. No source read says. Likely in a bank's savings-plan agreement (PDF) or the product page of a specific plan.
**Expansion of "פק"מ"** as used in Leumi product names: not found in any source read. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Closed by BANK-30 (institution strength).]**

**Official definition of prime.** Only bank definitions (Leumi, Hapoalim) were read; no BoI document; EDGE has no prime series (data-landscape 1.3.1). **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Still open. Searched: the web for a Bank of Israel definition or FAQ (only secondary sites say "BoI rate + 1.5%"); Directive 447 (it says "ריבית העוגן", no name); EDGE (no prime series). The BoI consumer pages are behind Radware and were not opened. Settles it: a BoI document that defines or reports prime. The general part of the old BANK-25 is BANK-25; the three banks' definitions are BANK-34.
**Hapoalim deposit product pages and concentrated publication**: the guessed URL /he/deposits returned 404; the home page links only to logged-in actions.
**Foreign bank branches and Altshuler Shaham Financial Services**: whether they take deposits from individuals in Israel.

Likely answer: the page in a browser or the Discount app; or the founder's paste. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Update: the page loads in a real browser, but Chrome auto-translated it; names not captured.]** **[2026-10-22 browser pass 2: Closed by BPN-12 (second browser pass, translation off).]**

**Mizrahi 447 table content** (the "שם הפיקדון" column, current-account interest). Same.
**FIBI-group PortalNG data source.** Whether online.fibi.co.il exposes a JSON endpoint behind "deposits-details"; Massad's code in the same app. Browser developer tools would show it.

**Bank of Jerusalem, One Zero, Esh Israel.** Blocked or no site. Browser by hand, or app screens typed in by a customer. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Partly closed by BPN-11 (Jerusalem, One Zero); Esh Israel still has no site.]**
**Pagi brand.** pagi.co.il is linked from Otzar's footer; whether it still sells deposits under its own names was not checked.
**Leumi PDF pages 40-68** were not read page by page (FX by currency assumed from pages 37-39 and 69-72).

Not stated in any source read. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: "פק"מ" closed by BANK-30; פז"ק, פקצ"מ, פח"ק, פצ"מ and הו"ק closed by BANK-31 (browser pass 3); לל"ת, מני"ע, Hapoalim's "(פ)" and Mercantile's פר"ן stay open.]**

**Hapoalim "חיסכון גמיש"** rate type and term: contract page 1 silent; the brochure https://www.bankhapoalim.co.il/sites/default/files/media/PDFS/פקדונות/gamish.pdf was seen only as a search result, not opened.

**FIBI and Massad shared names** (ארבל, איתן, סער, גולן; אופק vs אופק להשתלמות): one product or two; whether Otzar's sub-pages carry the same products.
**EDGE INTEREST_DASH series meaning**: codelist CL_BNK_WEB (about 1 MB) not decoded; reporting directive "D823A" not read. Likely in the BoI EDGE series browser.
**Fee-track names** at Mizrahi, Yahav, Massad, Jerusalem, One Zero not checked; Leumi "Total Digital"; Discount's 01-312 form is from 2015.

**Child-savings track names** at Discount (agreement 04-183 dated 01/01/17 seen only as a search result), Mercantile, Mizrahi (no NII page found), Massad (six plans unnamed), Otzar; Hapoalim's other five plan names (only one contract title read verbatim).
**Yahav 447 pages lag the board** (11_26 of 24/09/2026 inside board 13_26 of 06/10/2026): whether the 447 rows were current.
**App-only names**: every bank's app shows names after login that public pages may not (success criterion 5). Only the founder or a friend can supply them.
**Statement names**: whether Leumi statements show the "דגם" code; no statement was seen.

**Full TASE member list and the 3 unnamed Israeli non-bank members.** TASE counts 8 Israeli brokers; only 6 non-bank names appear in the clearing-house list. Tried tase.co.il/he/content/about/tase_members, market.tase.co.il/en/about_tase/tase_members/tase_members_list (JS shells), info.tase.co.il (DNS fails). Answer: a browser visit to the TASE member page, or TASE's members directory. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Closed by BRK-32.]**
**Status of the broker-dealer bill.** Only a 2024 press report was opened; search budget ran out. Answer: Knesset bill page or ISA publications.

**Current text of TASE rules on client assets (s.25, s.26) and any amendment after March 2018.** TASE rule book pages are JS-only. Answer: TASE "תקנון הבורסה" page in a browser, or TASE rule-book PDFs on content.tase.co.il.

**Other banks' securities custody terms.** Only Leumi was read. FIBI (פח-90 booklet), Otzar Hahayal and Pagi general-terms PDFs were seen in search results but not opened. **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Partly answered: the custody duties every bank carries are the Supervisor of Banks' (custody committee Q&A of 16.1.2013, Directive 461 s.6) and the TASE rules', BRK-10; no second bank's terms were read, so Leumi's pooling and lien terms stay Leumi's (BRK-47).

**What happens to a bank's clients' securities if the bank fails.** No official text found; the Banking Ordinance and the custody committee report are likely places. **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Still open, narrowed: the custody duties are now sourced (BRK-10), but neither the Supervisor's Q&A nor the TASE rules read say what happens in a bank's failure. The committee's full report was not reached (BoI press pages behind Radware, not worked around; no PDF found).

**The 2011 inter-ministerial custody committee report** (adopted by the Supervisor of Banks). Not opened; probably on boi.org.il or isa.gov.il. **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Partly answered: the joint press release of 2.1.2012 (recommendations listed), the Supervisor's adoption release and binding Q&A of 16.1.2013 were read (BRK-10); the report itself was identified but not opened.

**Interactive Brokers' own protection pages and the Irish Investor Compensation Company page.** interactivebrokers.com returned 403; investorcompensation.ie returned 307 redirects. Answer: browser visit. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Still open: interactivebrokers.com/en/accounts/protection.php now returns 404 (page moved).]** **[2026-10-22 browser pass 2: Closed by BRK-35.]**

**TASE's member-fee comparison under s.45טז.** market.tase.co.il/he/market_data/trading_fees (redirect target of tase.co.il/he/market_data/trading_fees) is a JS shell. Unknown: whether it shows list prices only or also actual-fee averages; this decides whether D4's "no reference available for non-bank brokers" holds. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Closed by BRK-33: the page shows average fees actually charged per member, banks and non-banks.]**

**Direct accounts at Interactive Brokers and eToro for Israeli residents.** Whether a foreign broker that does not solicit in Israel needs a 49A permit, and which entity serves Israelis. ISA pages and IBKR pages blocked; eToro's regulation page does not mention Israel. **[2026-10-25 foreign-broker pass: Narrowed for Interactive Brokers. Its pages open with curl now; its FAQ says the carrying entity follows the country of legal residence but does not name Israel's (BRK-43); its price list prices TASE, the LSE and US listings for direct clients (BRK-42). Still open: which IBKR entity serves an Israeli opening directly, whether a retail Israeli may trade TASE there, and whether IBKR holds or needs a 49A permit (the ISA's permit list was not found on the ISA site; a press aggregator was the only hit and is not a source). eToro not researched.]** **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Partly answered by the ISA: [רשות ניירות ערך: שאלות ותשובות בעקבות פרסום תנאי ההיתר הכללי לפי סעיף 49א (עדכון 13.1.2025)](https://www.new.isa.gov.il/images/Fittings/isa/asset_library_pic/al_lobby/al_lobby-626a5f3377ef9/QAA49a.pdf), p.3, question 5 "החוק אינו אוסר על פנייה של אדם ביוזמתו העצמית הבלעדית לגוף זר בבקשה לקבל ממנו שירותי מסחר בניירות ערך, אולם הדבר מותנה בכך שאותו הגוף כלל אינו פועל בישראל, לא ביצע כל פנייה לגורמים בישראל, והשירות יהיה מוגבל לזה שנעשתה פנייה לגביו" · checked 2026-10-25 · primary. A foreign broker that markets in Israel needs a s.49A permit (BRK-06). How the site presents "open an account at IBKR directly" in the light of this is for the founder. Still open: which IBKR entity serves an Israeli, and whether IBKR operates or solicits in Israel. **[2026-10-26 permit pass]** Narrowed: the permit is answered by the ISA's list (BRK-43): Interactive Brokers LLC and Interactive Brokers (U.K.) Limited hold section 49A permits since 20.10.2021, eToro (Europe) Ltd and eToro (UK) Ltd since 3.7.2022, so the own-initiative exception does not decide anything for them. Still open: which Interactive Brokers company carries an Israeli resident's direct account (the application with Israel as residence, or the top of an activity statement, would show it), and whether a retail Israeli may trade TASE there today. A person should also check, in a browser, whether the ISA site links a newer list than the August 2025 file.

**Whether a bank may charge a securities fee not listed in part 4** (for example a dividend-collection or monthly account fee on a securities account). The Banking (Service to Customer) Law (s.9 and following) was not opened.
**Custody fee on makam and money-market funds at non-bank members.** The bank ban (BRK-17) applies to banks; non-bank tariffs read do not mention an exemption.
**The supervised price for transferring securities to the client's own account elsewhere** ("(בפיקוח)"). Not in the rules; BoI supervised-price notices or each bank's tariff part 4(א)(6).
**Later amendments to the 1992 disclosure rules** after 30.12.2014, and the exact wording of s.5(א)(5) (read from a scanned page).
**Notice period for fee changes at non-bank members.** Not found in TASE rules read or in the tariffs (Psagot only says it may update fees from time to time).
**The rule that makes banks publish actual securities fees by size band** ("גילוי עלות שירותים בני"ע"). Probably a Supervisor of Banks directive; not found.

**Withholding by non-bank members and by foreign brokers.** No member page read states it; tax-file owners and broker account agreements are the likely sources. **[2026-10-22 browser pass 2: Partly: Interactive Israel says it withholds via HYBRID (BRK-36); other non-banks unchecked.]** **[2026-10-25 foreign-broker pass: Closed for the two foreign brokers as far as their own pages go: IBKR's tax page covers US withholding only (BRK-45) and no IBKR page mentions Israeli tax, so a direct account withholds nothing in Israel (TXF-22); Interactive Israel's HYBRID service is opt-in and its terms are in the BRK-36 note. Non-bank TASE members still unchecked.]** **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Closed for non-bank TASE members: the withholding regulations define the withholder, "מוסד כספי", as "תאגיד בנקאי או חבר בורסה" (TXS-05), so every TASE member withholds (BRK-27).
**Minors' brokerage accounts and joint-account rules beyond Leumi's section heading.** Not found on any page read.

**Meitav Trade tariff.** Not linked from meitav.co.il/trade, the independent-trading page or the terms page; meitavtrade.co.il redirects to meitav.co.il/trade/independent_trading/. **[2026-10-24 R4 research pass: Still open. A Google search of meitav.co.il/trade for 'תעריפון' finds no tariff; the tracks page gives words, not figures (Institutions table); TASE's calculator shows Meitav Trade's list fee (BRK-33) but its terms bar republishing (BRK-37). The snapshot stays `missing: true`.]**
**One Zero brokerage offer and tariff.** onezerobank.com returns 403. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Closed by BRK-34.]**

**Psagot brokerage ownership after the 2024 transactions** (domain open question 16). Psagot's home and about pages do not name owners; TASE guide confirms "Psagot Securities Ltd." as a clearing member.

**Fractional shares and order types that change cost.** No provider page read mentions fractional shares; TASE trading guide (part three of the rules, `content.tase.co.il/media/mwsduioc/274698.pdf`) not opened.
Domain open questions from `research/discovery/domain-landscape.md` section 8: **2** partly closed (BRK-02, BRK-03; three names still open, Q1 above); **14** closed for where tariffs are published except Meitav Trade, One Zero and Interactive Israel (BRK-30, Institutions); **15** partly closed (Interactive Israel's 49A permit and non-supervision, BRK-06; its entity choice and what it offers, BRK-41; direct IBKR's price list and entity rule, BRK-42 and BRK-43, with the 49A question and the entity for Israelis still open, Q9; eToro still open); **16** still open (Q20).

**hly.gov.il blocked.** The current official list of approved funds and banks, and NII's track descriptions, are on hly.gov.il. NII's sub-pages redirect there, and it returned 403 to scripts on 2026-10-22: https://hly.gov.il/ProvidentFunds.html, https://hly.gov.il/banksManageInfo.html, https://hly.gov.il/Differences.html, https://hly.gov.il/. Next step: read it in a browser. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Closed: hly.gov.il opens in a browser (CS-24, CS-25).]**

**Clal.** Is Clal on the approved provident list, since when, and through which tender? Gemel-Net 202609 has four Clal child-savings tracks with inception 2026-03-09 and very small TOTAL_ASSETS values, while NII's end-2025 report lists 9 funds without Clal. The answer is probably on hly.gov.il or in a Ministry of Finance tender notice. The web-search budget ran out before this could be searched further. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: Closed by CS-24: Clal is on NII's official list.]**

**Amendments to the 2016 regulations.** The Wikisource copy shows no amendments. Yet the default rules changed in 2020, 2022 and 2025, and law 74ב(ד)(1א) and (2א) were added. It is not known which instrument sets the default track. The answer is probably in the Knesset legislation database or Reshumot (Kovetz Takanot). **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Partly answered: the track inside the fund is set by CMA circular 2022-9-29 s.3(ד)-(ד2) (CS-07, CS-26); the instrument behind NII's fund-level default was not found.

**First child's default fund.** How is the default fund for a first child picked today? The 2016 regulation 3(ב) used a fixed rotation, and Altshuler's page says rotation, but NII's current pages and report do not say. The answer is probably on hly.gov.il or in an amended regulation 3. **[2026-10-23 R3 research pass: Still open. NII's newborn page and FAQ give the track (increased risk) but not how the manager is picked (CS-26).]**

**Legal source of the age-18 grant (born up to 2016).** The current law 74ג(ב) mentions only the age-21 sum, and 74ג(א) was repealed. The age-18 grant is stated by NII and in bank agreements. The source is probably a transitional provision of amendment תשע"ז־9; its text was not read.

**Medical early withdrawal.** Law 74ד(ב) (read as a mirror summary) says the age-3 and age-13 sums are added. NII's page says a NIS 582 grant is deposited. Which applies to which birth cohort? Next step: read the verbatim 74ד(ב) and NII's medical-withdrawal procedure.

**Track definitions at other managers.** Only Harel's bylaw was read: equity 75%–120% in the increased-risk track, with the low and medium tracks at committee discretion. Are all managers' bylaws a uniform "standard bylaw" set by the CMA, and what equity range does each manager's low and medium track have? The answer is in each manager's bylaw and the CMA circular on the standard bylaw (gov.il, blocked for scripts). **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Partly answered: the CMA standard child bylaw (annex to circular 2016-9-20) leaves each track's investment policy blank for the company, and circular 2022-9-29 s.3(ב) has each manager set it, approved by the Commissioner (CS-09, CS-26). Each manager's equity range still needs its own bylaw.

**Fee after 21 at every manager.** 0.23% of balance is sourced for Harel (bylaw) and Altshuler (Q&A) only. The bylaw cap "דמי הניהול השנתי המרבי הקבוע בהסדר התחיקתי" has no figure here; it belongs to PF. Next step: read the bylaws of the other managers. **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Partly answered: the cap after 21 is the fee regulations' reg. 2, 1.05% of the balance and 4% of deposits (CS-18). Each manager's rate is still open (Harel and Altshuler Shaham: CS-30).

**Gemel-Net fee field for child-savings tracks.** AVG_ANNUAL_MANAGEMENT_FEE is 0 to 0.02 (or null) for all 41 tracks, while NII pays 0.23%. Is the field the fee charged to members (zero before 21), and in what unit? This is the same as discovery O11.

**Can a parent see whether the child's track was chosen or defaulted?** Funds report this to NII (CS-20), but no statement field or NII-page field was found that shows it to the parent. This directly blocks product.md 3.6. Possible places: the NII personal-information page (needs an ID), the annual statement, the manager's personal area. **[2026-10-23 R3 research pass: Narrowed. The annual statement template has no such field (CS-27); NII's personal-information service exists but needs the parent's ID, so it was not checked (CS-26).]**

**Annual statement layout for child savings.** The fields and labels were not found. The statement follows the Commissioner's format (Harel s.27). The answer is probably in the CMA circular on annual reports (PF) and a sample statement. **[2026-10-23 R3 research pass: Closed by CS-27 (annex ב'ג' of circular 2018-9-25).]**

**Per-bank terms.** Only Yahav's agreement (undated, 2017-era figures) was read. Leumi's terms PDF (https://www.leumi.co.il/leumi-hebrew/s3fs-public/2023-06/SavingsForEachChild/terms_25.07.18.pdf), FIBI's (https://www.fibi.co.il/media/ypgewotq/הסכם-חיסכון.pdf) and Massad's (https://www.bankmassad.co.il/media/23kock3b/פ-409-מסד-הסכם-לפתיחת-חשבון-חיסכון-כולל-מדיניות-הפרטיות-2-26.pdf) appeared in search results but were not opened. Current rates are also missing, because the MoF dataset stops at 02/09/2025 (CS-23).

**After 18 or 21: moving into another product.** Can the child move the money into a regular (non-child) investment provident fund, or into another product, or add their own deposits? Regulation 11(ב) allows transfers "בין קופות גמל להשקעה", and it is unclear whether this is limited to child-savings funds. The bylaw allows deposits by NII only. The answer is probably in the CMA transfer rules (PF) and the manager's service pages.

~~**Bank-to-provident move: amendment and effective date.**~~ Closed 2026-10-25: NII's consolidated law text, p.50, footnote 32: s.74ב(א)(2א) was added by amendment 247, in force 1.1.2025 (CS-12). Earlier note: the law text was from the mirror without a per-paragraph amendment note. NII's report says January 2025 and Altshuler says 1.1.2025. Next step: the Knesset amendment text. **[2026-10-22 browser pass: See CS-25: NII's page says bank money cannot move to a provident fund.]**
**Retroactive parental addition.** Can a parent who turns on the addition late make up past months? No source says so. Sources only say it starts the month after the request.

**KGL rules that may or may not apply.** Does the general investment-provident-fund deposit ceiling or any other KGL rule apply to child-savings funds? Not found. This belongs to the KGL and PF owners. **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Partly answered: circular 2022-9-29 s.1 applies every provision for kupat gemel lehashkaa to the child-savings fund (CS-18); whether the yearly deposit ceiling bites was not read.

**Later amendments to the child-savings circular 2016-9-20.** Only the 2018-9-25 amendment (with its annexes) was read. Likely answer: the CMA regulation engine on gov.il. **[2026-10-25 scope pass]** Answered: two later amendments, 2019-9-17 (https://www.gov.il/BlobFolder/dynamiccollectorresultitem/regulation-541/he/regulation_h_2019-9-17.docx, not read) and 2022-9-29 (read: CS-07, CS-26, CS-18).

**Registered rating companies.** Which companies are registered with the ISA under the 2014 rating law today. Tried: one web search (no official list), Midroog home and "about" pages (no registration statement), maalot.co.il (403). Likely place: the ISA's registers ("מאגרים ומרשמים"), or each agency's regulatory-disclosure page.

**Registered trustees.** Names of the companies in the ISA trustees register. Tried: one web search, which returned only law-firm summaries and one bank trust company's page. Likely place: the ISA registers.

**S&P Maalot scale definitions**, and the exact quorum and majority for a holders' acceleration decision (s. 35ט1(ד)), which was only read in summary. Tried: maalot.co.il (403). Likely place: S&P Maalot's definitions PDF; a full read of s. 35ט1 on Wikisource or Nevo. **[2026-10-24 R5 pass: the quorum half is closed (CORP-07 annotation: 50% attendance, majority of the face value voting, 20% at an adjourned meeting). maalot.co.il now loads a reCAPTCHA shell to scripts; the definitions need a browser.]**
**Is a rating mandatory** for a public bond offering, a TASE listing, or listed commercial paper? Nothing read says so. Likely place: TASE rules part 2 (listing) and ISA prospectus regulations.

**Public tender in practice.** Is the 2007 offering regulations text current (Wikisource shows amendments only to 2016)? How does an individual's order reach a bond tender (through a TASE member), with what minimum and fee? Are bond tenders run on price, interest rate or spread? Likely place: Nevo (current text), TASE offering procedures, bank tariffs (BRK-16 line), a bank's "הנפקות" help page.

**TASE trading details for bonds:** how prices are quoted (agorot per NIS 1 or per 100 face value), the settlement cycle, ex-date and record date for coupons, and the criteria for the maintenance and low-liquidity lists, including delisting of bonds. The TASE trading guide was read for units, phases and last trading day only. Likely place: the rest of guide 274698, TASE rules part 2 and part 3, clearing-house rules.
**TASE-UP and institutional-only securities:** what they are and whether an individual can buy them. Seen only as labels in the TASE report and guide.

**Tel-Bond methodology:** the current rules document, index list (Tel-Bond 20/40/60, Tel-Bond Shekel, sub-indices), thresholds and weights. Tried: one web search (only press and 2015/2016 composition notices). Likely place: the TASE indices pages or methodology PDFs on content.tase.co.il.

Question 5 (death before 75) has an institution answer (TXA-26 annotation).
- **Executive insurance: blocked.** Deposit and annuity rules are the pension rules (TXA-12, TXA-13). Blocking: open question 6 (tax on growth inside an insurance fund), 7 (risk and disability components, death split); 8 matters for pre-2008 capital policies.
- **Amendment 190 deposits: partly unblocked.** Closed and primary: what money qualifies (TXA-17), exemption from 60 (TXA-18), 15% of the nominal relative profit on commutation (TXA-19, the rate in Q6), when commutation is lawful (TXA-20). Blocking: open questions 9 and 10 (the age ceilings, the benefited layer and the age-60 and payslip conditions rest on fund documents only; D10 names primary, secondary and open but not institution-strength rules, so a product decision is needed on whether those compute), 11 (interaction with the exempt commutation), 14 and 15 (NII and surtax on the result). *2026-10-24:* the payslip condition is now primary (TXA-27, circular 2/2013); the age ceilings (9) are still institution only: a secondary source (Adif, Cloudflare-blocked to scripts) attributes them to a Tax Authority ruling ("החלטת מיסוי"), which a browser pass should locate on gov.il.
